sectors.trend: Mixed: miners fall on ASX broadly (headline 16) but gold sub-sector strong with multiple WA/Qld discoveries; coal boom supports energy miners; lithium exploration (ZhongNuo/Chariot in Nigeria) signals long-term demand; McLaren titanium grades surge at WA project
sectors.implications: Gold miners (AUC.AX, GRY.AX, KGA.AX) and coal names (BHP.AX, WDS.AX, BOQ.AX) are relative outperformers. Diversify away from iron ore exposure given global demand uncertainty. Lithium (LGS.AX, SGO.AX) remains speculative near-term.

sectors.trend: Banks fall on ASX (headline 16); CBA fee controversy (headline 37) dents reputation; mortgage stress at 18-year highs (headline 17) raises NPL concerns; rate hike expectations support net interest margin but credit risk looms
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face margin pressure from credit deterioration. Housing-linked exposure is the key vulnerability. Monitor NPL trends and RBA policy path.

sectors.trend: Oil at two-month high on US-Iran strikes (headlines 32, 43); coal boom in Australia (headline 58); inflation risk from energy prices feeds rate-hike fears
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, BOQ.AX, AWE.AX benefit from oil/coal strength. However, higher energy costs feed domestic inflation, complicating RBA's path and pressuring rate-sensitive sectors.

sectors.trend: Severe stress: housing 'bloodbath' predicted (headline 40), 10% price fall forecast (headline 39), Bathla near collapse (headline 76), 'Evergrande moment' (headline 31), mortgage stress at 18-year highs
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, DGL.AX, ICPS.AX) and property developers face significant downside. Consumer staples (WES.AX, WOL.AX) offer relative defensiveness. Avoid speculative property plays.

sectors.trend: No major ASX-specific headlines; global AI capex shocker (headline 62) and Iran 'bombing AI bubble' (headline 25) create volatility in tech globally; Canva privacy dispute (headline 41) minor
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX remain defensive anchors. Global tech volatility may spill into ASX small-cap tech. Maintain defensive healthcare allocation.

sectors.trend: Qantas ground crews vote for strike right (headline 75); Jetstar first flight to Western Sydney Airport (headline 53) positive for Qantas group
sectors.implications: QAN.AX faces near-term industrial risk. Western Sydney Airport (WSS) is a long-term infrastructure catalyst. Monitor Qantas industrial action escalation.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain under pressure over 1–3 months. Oil-driven inflation and 4th RBA rate hike risk weigh on rate-sensitive sectors. Housing stress and developer defaults create contagion risk for banks. Geopolitical (US-Iran) volatility sustains risk-off sentiment. Gold and energy are relative outperformers. Expect elevated VIX and AUD weakness.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautious. Productivity 'bad to worse' and per-capita recession risk cap earnings growth. Housing correction (10% decline) will drag consumer spending and bank credit. However, commodity strength (coal, gold) and export earnings provide partial offset. RBA likely to peak rates by Q1 2027, creating a turning point. Structural productivity reform is the key long-term variable.
